paragraphs: Planning can help a reinforcement learning agent choose better actions by considering possible futures. But when a planner selects the actions used to collect experience, those actions can differ from what the agent's policy would choose itself. The paper addresses this mismatch, which can interfere with learning both the environment model and the policy.

BOOM connects the policy and planner in a repeating learning loop. The policy supplies initial actions, and the planner improves them. A jointly trained world model supports this process by simulating future trajectories and supplying value targets. The policy then learns to align its behavior with the planner through a loss that does not require an explicit likelihood for the planner's action distribution.

Because stored planner actions vary in quality, BOOM also uses soft value weighting to emphasize behaviors associated with higher returns. Experiments on DeepMind Control Suite and Humanoid-Bench report state-of-the-art training stability and final performance. These findings support tighter coordination between planning and policy learning in the evaluated control tasks.
neurips-2025-bootstrap-off-policy-with-w.tldr: BOOM links a policy, planner, and learned world model in a feedback loop that improves reinforcement learning stability and performance.

paragraphs: Garments are difficult for robots to handle because their shapes change during manipulation, and different garments can require different contact points and movements. DexGarmentLab provides a simulation environment specifically for dexterous garment handling, especially with two hands. It includes high-quality 3D assets covering 15 task scenarios and garment simulation refinements intended to reduce differences between simulation and reality.

The paper also addresses the cost of collecting demonstrations. It uses structural correspondences between garments to generate varied trajectories from a single expert demonstration. This reduces manual work, but the authors recognize that demonstrations cannot cover every possible garment configuration. Their policy therefore needs to transfer what it learns to unfamiliar shapes and deformations.

The proposed HALO policy divides manipulation into two stages: identifying transferable points suitable for action, then generating a trajectory to complete the task. Experiments report that HALO consistently outperforms existing methods and handles unseen garments with substantial shape and deformation changes. The contribution combines an environment, a demonstration expansion method, and a policy designed around this generalization challenge.
neurips-2025-dexgarmentlab-dexterous-gar.tldr: DexGarmentLab combines dexterous garment simulation, automatic demonstration expansion, and a hierarchical policy that generalizes to unfamiliar garment shapes.

paragraphs: Hashing-based retrieval represents items with compact binary codes, allowing efficient storage and similarity search. Domain adaptation extends this approach from a labeled source collection to an unlabeled target collection. The goal is to keep semantically similar target items close in binary-code space, even when their data distribution differs from the source.

The paper identifies two obstacles: automatically assigned labels can be noisy, and adapting only one representation space leaves useful information underused. VPDS uses a pretrained vision-language model to calibrate these pseudo-labels, drawing on its ability to generalize without target-specific labeled examples. This calibration is intended to reduce bias in the labels that guide adaptation.

VPDS also aligns the source and target domains separately in two spaces. The richer feature space carries semantic information, while the compact binary space supports efficient discrimination and retrieval. Experiments on three benchmark datasets report consistent improvements over existing methods in both cross-domain and single-domain retrieval. The findings support addressing label quality and representation alignment together, while preserving the compact codes that make hashing useful.
neurips-2025-domain-adaptive-hashing-ret.tldr: VPDS improves compact image retrieval by using a vision-language model to refine pseudo-labels and adapting both feature and binary-code spaces.

paragraphs: This paper studies optimization problems with several difficulties at once: noisy information, objectives that can have multiple local solutions, nonsmooth behavior, and constraints that place valid solutions on a curved mathematical space. Its central question is how many samples an algorithm needs to reach a precisely defined form of approximate stationarity.

The authors first extend Goldstein stationarity to Riemannian manifolds, providing a performance criterion suited to nonsmooth objectives under these geometric constraints. They then introduce Riemannian Online to NonConvex, or RO2NC. The analysis establishes a sample complexity of O(ε⁻³δ⁻¹) for finding a (δ, ε)-stationary point. The parameters specify the approximation criterion; the guarantee concerns stationarity rather than global optimality.

The abstract describes this as the first finite-time guarantee for fully nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization on manifolds, matching the optimal Euclidean complexity. A zeroth-order variant, designed for settings without gradient information, receives the same stated complexity bound. Numerical experiments support the analysis and demonstrate practical effectiveness, connecting the theoretical guarantees with observed algorithm behavior.
neurips-2025-finite-time-analysis-of-sto.tldr: RO2NC provides finite-time stationarity guarantees for noisy, nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization on manifolds, including a version without gradients.

paragraphs: Attention flow examines how information moves through multiple Transformer layers, offering a broader view than inspecting attention within one layer. Its computational cost comes from running maximum-flow algorithms on the attention graph. FlowPrune aims to make this analysis cheaper while retaining close agreement with the original attention-flow results.

The method simplifies the graph before computing flow. It uses the Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem together with two structural properties of Transformers to identify regions that are not critical to the calculation. Edge Pruning removes attention connections judged insignificant, while Layer Compression removes layers whose contributions to the flow are small. Both components reduce the graph that the expensive calculation must process.

Experiments on LLaMA and LLaVA report high agreement with the original method in absolute and relative errors and in the input tokens identified as influential. Language and vision case studies also produce consistent interpretability outcomes. These results support FlowPrune as an efficient approximation for attention-flow analysis in the evaluated models, preserving useful explanatory patterns while reducing computational work.
neurips-2025-flowprune-accelerating-atte.tldr: FlowPrune speeds up attention-flow analysis by removing low-contribution edges and layers while closely preserving the original results.

paragraphs: Physical measurements often sample only a small number of irregular locations and times. Reconstructing an entire evolving field from those observations is difficult for generative methods built around fixed spatial and temporal grids. SDIFT addresses this mismatch by representing dynamics in a space designed to accommodate continuous positions and sparse observations.

Its representation uses a functional Tucker model, combining latent functions with sequences of compact core tensors. The paper establishes a universal approximation property for this representation. A sequential diffusion model then generates core-tensor sequences by denoising Gaussian-process noise, using a UNet augmented to model temporal structure. This places the generative process inside the functional representation rather than directly on a preset observation grid.

A message-passing posterior sampling mechanism lets observations at a limited number of times guide generation of the full sequence. The authors evaluate SDIFT on supernova explosions, ocean sound-speed fields, and an organic liquid system. They report substantial improvements in reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency over state-of-the-art approaches across these three physical settings.
neurips-2025-generating-full-field-evolu.tldr: SDIFT reconstructs evolving physical fields from sparse, irregular observations using sequential diffusion in a continuous functional representation.

paragraphs: Continuous-time equations can make optimization algorithms easier to analyze, but an algorithm actually updates its parameters in discrete steps. The difference between those steps and a continuous approximation can affect what the analysis reveals. This paper focuses on that discretization gap for the Heavy-Ball momentum method.

The authors construct a first-order, piecewise continuous differential equation and add correction terms that explicitly account for discretization error. Their construction allows the error to be controlled to arbitrary order in the learning rate. The contribution is therefore a more adjustable mathematical approximation of Heavy-Ball dynamics, with explicit control over how closely the continuous model tracks the discrete method.

The paper uses this framework to identify an implicit regularization effect involving directional smoothness. It also investigates the implicit bias of Heavy-Ball training in diagonal linear networks, showing how the approximation can help study learning behavior beyond the update equations alone. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results. These applications illustrate how careful treatment of discretization can reveal properties that a less precise continuous approximation may not capture.
neurips-2025-heavy-ball-momentum-method-.tldr: A corrected continuous-time model of Heavy-Ball momentum controls discretization error and reveals implicit regularization and bias.

paragraphs: A generated video can look convincing while depicting motion or events that do not make physical sense. PhysHPO addresses this gap through preference optimization that evaluates several aspects of a video separately. Its goal is to improve physical plausibility alongside the broader quality of generated content.

The framework organizes alignment into four levels. At the instance level, it matches the overall video to the prompt. At the state level, it uses boundary frames as anchors for temporal consistency. At the motion level, it models trajectories for realistic dynamics. At the semantic level, it seeks agreement between the narrative and what appears on screen. Together, these levels provide more detailed training guidance than a single overall preference.

The authors also introduce an automated pipeline that selects useful examples from existing large-scale text-video datasets, drawing on real videos as evidence of physical behavior. Experiments on physics-focused and general benchmarks report significant improvements in physical plausibility and overall generation quality. The results support combining finer preference signals with targeted data selection to improve advanced video models.
neurips-2025-hierarchical-fine-grained-p.tldr: PhysHPO improves video plausibility through preference training across content, temporal states, motion, and semantics, supported by automated data selection.

paragraphs: 3D Gaussian Splatting can render new views of a scene quickly and with high quality, but its standard color representation has limited capacity. Fine spatial detail and appearance changes with viewpoint, such as specular highlights, are especially challenging. Adding texture maps can help, but the alternatives described in the paper face either scene-complexity difficulties or substantial storage costs.

Image-Based Gaussian Splatting uses high-resolution source images to supply detail and view-specific appearance. For each rendered pixel, it combines the base color from standard Gaussian Splatting with a learned correction inferred from neighboring training images. This residual formulation supplements the existing renderer with image-based information where its basic color model is insufficient.

The approach promotes accurate alignment with scene surfaces while representing fine detail and effects that depend on viewing direction. On standard novel-view synthesis benchmarks, the authors report significantly better rendering quality than prior Gaussian Splatting methods without increasing the storage footprint. The findings show that the source images can contribute richer appearance information within an efficient rendering representation.
neurips-2025-ibgs-image-based-gaussian-s.tldr: IBGS adds image-derived color corrections to Gaussian Splatting, improving fine details and view-dependent appearance without increasing storage.

paragraphs: Language-model applications often reuse the same documents across different questions, yet repeatedly encode those documents as part of each new input. KVLink reduces this redundant work by computing each document's key-value cache independently in advance. At inference time, the system joins the caches for the retrieved documents instead of encoding their contents again.

Independent encoding creates a challenge: the cached documents were not processed together in their final positions. KVLink addresses this in two ways. It adjusts positional embeddings to reflect each cache's position after concatenation, and it introduces trainable special tokens that restore self-attention across the separately encoded documents. These changes aim to preserve useful interactions while retaining the computational savings of reuse.

Across seven datasets, the authors report an average 4% improvement in question-answering accuracy over state-of-the-art methods. They also report up to a 96% reduction in time to the first generated token compared with standard inference. KVLink can additionally work with cache compression, reducing storage and loading overhead while continuing to outperform the evaluated baselines.
neurips-2025-kvlink-accelerating-large-l.tldr: KVLink reuses independently cached documents while repairing their positions and cross-document attention, improving accuracy and reducing response startup time.

paragraphs: Diffusion generation can be accelerated by reducing the number of integration steps, but numerical solvers can struggle in the very low-step regime, while distillation can add complexity and instability. This paper proposes learning how to integrate the diffusion model's ordinary differential equation, aiming for a useful balance between generation quality and computational cost.

The training losses come from the relationship between derivatives and integrals, with inspiration from Monte Carlo integration and Picard iteration. Geometrically, the method extends information about a tangent, which describes local change, toward a secant, which describes change across an interval. The authors therefore call them secant losses. Their targets match either the original diffusion-training target or the diffusion model itself, which the paper associates with strong training stability.

Using fine-tuning or distillation, the secant version of EDM reaches an FID of 2.14 with ten steps on CIFAR-10. The secant version of SiT-XL/2 reaches FIDs of 2.27 with four steps and 1.96 with eight steps on ImageNet at 256 by 256 resolution. These results demonstrate generation with small integration-step budgets.
neurips-2025-learning-to-integrate-diffu.tldr: Secant losses teach diffusion models to integrate across larger intervals, enabling stable training for generation with few steps.

paragraphs: Computer-use agents need to operate across different applications, operating systems, and languages. Existing interactive benchmarks leave an important gap around macOS and emphasize English. macOSWorld addresses that gap with tasks designed around the operating system's distinctive interface conventions and applications, providing a more targeted test of agent capabilities.

The benchmark contains 202 interactive tasks across 30 applications, including 28 exclusive to macOS. Both task instructions and operating-system interfaces are available in English, Chinese, Arabic, Japanese, and Russian. A dedicated safety subset also evaluates vulnerability to deception attacks, extending the assessment beyond whether an agent can complete an ordinary task.

Evaluation of six agents finds a large performance divide: proprietary computer-use agents exceed 30% success, while lightweight open-source research models remain below 5%. The multilingual results reveal further weaknesses, especially an average 28.8% degradation in Arabic relative to English. Safety results also indicate broader susceptibility to deception. Together, these findings identify macOS adaptation, language coverage, and resilience to misleading content as distinct challenges exposed by the benchmark.
neurips-2025-macosworld-a-multilingual-i.tldr: macOSWorld tests computer-use agents across macOS applications and five languages, revealing substantial capability, multilingual, and deception-resilience gaps.

paragraphs: Model merging combines trained model checkpoints, and this paper investigates how that technique can help during language-model pretraining. The focus is on using merging within the training process itself, where its potential has been less thoroughly explored. The study covers both dense models and Mixture-of-Experts architectures.

The experiments span models with millions of parameters through models with more than 100 billion. A central finding concerns checkpoints trained at constant learning rates: merging them produces significant performance improvements and enables accurate prediction of annealing behavior. Annealing refers to reducing the learning rate during training, so this predictive ability connects checkpoint merging with decisions about how training should proceed.

The authors report that these benefits make model development more efficient and substantially reduce training costs. They also vary merging strategies and hyperparameters to investigate which choices matter and to examine the mechanisms behind the results. The resulting guidance is intended to help the open-source community apply merging during pretraining. The evidence supports merging as a practical training-process tool across the studied model scales and architectures.
neurips-2025-model-merging-in-pre-traini.tldr: Merging constant-learning-rate checkpoints improves language-model pretraining performance and helps predict annealing behavior, reducing development and training costs.

paragraphs: Low-rank methods reduce the number of independent quantities needed to represent a model's weight matrices. They are successful for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, but maintaining useful low-rank structure during pretraining is more difficult. Q3R addresses this problem with a regularizer designed to encourage prescribed low target ranks during training.

The method draws on iteratively reweighted least squares. Its quadratic penalty upper-bounds a smoothed log-determinant objective that serves as a substitute for directly optimizing matrix rank. This gives training a way to encourage low-rank weights while remaining compatible with existing model architectures. The authors report small computational overhead and predictive performance comparable to dense models.

In a ViT-Tiny experiment on CIFAR-10, the method allows 60% of parameters to be removed with only marginal performance loss. Removing up to 80% produces a reported 4% accuracy drop. Experiments also cover Transformers in image and language tasks, including low-rank fine-tuning. These results support Q3R as a way to build compressible weight structure during learning while controlling the resulting performance tradeoff.
neurips-2025-q3r-quadratic-reweighted-ra.tldr: Q3R encourages prescribed low-rank weights during training, enabling substantial parameter reduction with modest reported performance losses.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can help address causal confusion and distribution shifts associated with imitation learning, but training a driving policy directly from raw sensors remains difficult. Model-based methods offer a promising route, although they commonly depend on privileged inputs. Raw2Drive uses a two-stream training approach to connect privileged-information learning with a sensor-based driving policy.

The first stream trains an auxiliary world model and neural planner using privileged information. The second introduces a world model that operates on raw sensor data. A guidance mechanism keeps the two world models consistent during rollouts, allowing the sensor-based model to benefit from the easier-to-train privileged stream. Knowledge contained in the privileged model's prediction heads then helps guide sensor-policy training.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on CARLA Leaderboard 2.0 and Bench2Drive, and describe Raw2Drive as the only reinforcement-learning-based end-to-end method on those benchmarks at the time of the paper. The contribution is a training pathway that transfers guidance between aligned world models, making model-based reinforcement learning applicable to the evaluated raw-sensor driving setting.
neurips-2025-raw2drive-reinforcement-lea.tldr: Raw2Drive trains a raw-sensor driving policy by aligning its world model with an auxiliary model trained on privileged information.

paragraphs: Irregular time series contain observations whose positions do not fit a simple uniform sequence. Transformers often handle them through specialized architecture changes, which can add complexity and computation. RoMAE instead extends a masked autoencoder using rotary positional embeddings that support continuous positions, including positions with multiple dimensions.

This positional representation allows the model to perform interpolation and learn representations without time-series-specific architectural components. The authors evaluate the same general approach across irregular and multivariate time series, images, and audio. On difficult time-series datasets, including the DESC ELAsTiCC Challenge, RoMAE outperforms specialized architectures while maintaining the usual masked-autoencoder performance in other modalities.

The paper also examines whether the model can reconstruct the continuous positions represented by its embeddings. That analysis reveals that including learned embeddings in the input sequence breaks the relative-position property associated with rotary positional embeddings. Alongside the empirical results, this finding clarifies how positional information can behave inside the architecture. The work therefore contributes both a broadly applicable representation-learning method and an observation about the interaction between learned inputs and rotary positions.
neurips-2025-rotary-masked-autoencoders-.tldr: RoMAE uses continuous rotary positions to extend masked autoencoders across irregular time series and other modalities without specialized time-series architectures.

paragraphs: Human preference datasets can contain incorrect judgments, such as labels favoring a less desirable response. This paper studies alignment objectives that remain robust to severe label noise through a property called redescending. In the paper's formulation, this means retaining the same model parameters despite that noise; the authors prove that existing alignment methods do not satisfy the property.

They introduce Hölder-DPO, an alignment loss with a provable redescending property. The resulting aligned model estimates the clean-data likelihood, which also provides a metric for valuing feedback data. This metric can identify where mislabeled examples occur and estimate their fraction. It requires neither gradient calculations nor a clean validation dataset, supporting automated evaluation without costly manual checking.

The authors report state-of-the-art robust alignment performance and accurate mislabel detection on controlled datasets. Applied to Anthropic HH-RLHF, the method identifies substantial noise, and removing the identified mislabels significantly improves alignment across methods. The contribution connects robust training with dataset assessment: a model trained to withstand corrupted feedback also supplies evidence for finding problematic labels.
neurips-2025-scalable-valuation-of-human.tldr: Hölder-DPO combines provably robust preference alignment with a scalable metric for detecting and valuing noisy human feedback.

paragraphs: Finding an image's precise location becomes difficult when the search area spans a continent. Searching enormous ground-image collections is costly and depends on adequate coverage. Broad geographic classification tends to give coarse answers, while matching ground photographs to aerial images must bridge substantial visual differences. This paper combines classification-based learning with retrieval to address these tradeoffs.

During training, a proxy classification task teaches feature representations that implicitly retain precise location information. The method then combines the resulting learned prototypes with representations of aerial imagery. This combination is designed to make localization more robust where ground-level imagery is sparse, while supporting direct, fine-grained retrieval across multiple countries.

On a dataset covering a large portion of Europe, the approach places more than 68% of query images within 200 meters of their locations. This is a continent-scale empirical result, rather than a claim that precise global localization has been solved. It shows that classification-derived representations and aerial information can work together to achieve substantially finer localization than coarse geographic classes alone.
neurips-2025-scaling-image-geo-localizat.tldr: A hybrid of classification-trained prototypes and aerial-image representations localizes over 68% of queries within 200 meters on a large European dataset.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised graph anomaly detection uses a small set of labeled normal nodes to identify unusual nodes among many unlabeled ones. Existing methods often assume that normal nodes share similar patterns of homophily, or similarity between connected nodes. They also assume the labeled examples adequately represent those patterns. The paper argues that real normal nodes can be considerably more varied.

RHO learns this variation through two components. Adaptive frequency response filters capture different graph-frequency components of the labeled normal nodes, examining attributes both within individual channels and across channels. Graph normality alignment then encourages consistency between these two views. The combination aims to learn a more robust representation of normal behavior from limited labels.

Across eight real-world graph anomaly datasets, RHO substantially outperforms state-of-the-art competing methods. The authors report that it learns varying homophily patterns, including patterns poorly represented in the small labeled set. These findings support treating normality as structurally diverse: nodes can differ in their neighborhood relationships without those differences necessarily indicating an anomaly.
neurips-2025-semi-supervised-graph-anoma.tldr: RHO improves graph anomaly detection by learning diverse normal-node similarity patterns and aligning complementary views of those patterns.

paragraphs: Strategic classification studies prediction when people can change their input features, at some cost, in response to a classifier. The model therefore influences the data it will later see. Most prior analysis has focused on linear classifiers; this paper examines how nonlinear decision rules alter the interaction between a classifier and strategic users.

The authors build their analysis from decision-boundary behavior to expressive power and model-class complexity. They find that strategic responses can either increase or decrease the effective complexity of a nonlinear classifier class. The decrease can be arbitrarily large. Thus, the flexibility available before users respond does not by itself determine the flexibility of the resulting strategic system.

A further result concerns universal approximators, including neural networks: their usual universality no longer holds once the environment is strategic. Empirical demonstrations show that this can create performance gaps even with an unrestricted model class. The findings identify strategic response as a fundamental part of the learning problem, with consequences that cannot be inferred simply from a model's ordinary approximation capacity.
neurips-2025-strategic-classification-wi.tldr: Strategic user responses can reshape nonlinear classifier complexity and remove the universality ordinarily associated with neural networks.

paragraphs: This paper studies how a standard Transformer can solve combinatorial problems through structured trial and error. Sudoku serves as the main task, allowing the authors to combine simple logical rules with explicit search. Their model is a vanilla decoder-only GPT-2, operating without external tools, function calls, or a custom problem-specific architecture.

Training combines imitation of basic Sudoku rules with depth-first search. The search process includes informed guesses and backtracking, so a failed choice can be revisited instead of forcing the model to continue down an unproductive path. The authors also move beyond imitating demonstrations by targeting the number of guesses required to reach a solution.

The method achieves 99% accuracy, which the paper reports as state of the art relative to prior neuro-symbolic approaches. For theoretical analysis, the authors connect the guess-minimization objective to a contextual version of Min-Sum Set Cover. This gives a formal framework for studying search efficiency. Although the broader motivation concerns problems in NP, the stated experimental achievement is specifically demonstrated through Sudoku.
neurips-2025-teaching-transformers-to-so.tldr: A standard GPT-2 learns Sudoku rules, guessing, and backtracking, reaching 99% accuracy while targeting more efficient search.

paragraphs: TIDMAD makes data from the ABRACADABRA dark-matter experiment available for developing and evaluating AI denoising methods. The experiment records ten million samples per second, producing extremely long time series. A dark-matter signal, if present in this search, would appear as a sinusoidal oscillation within those measurements, making signal extraction the central computational task.

The release combines three components. It provides training, validation, and science subsets of the time-series data; a denoising score for comparing models directly; and a complete analysis framework that turns processed measurements into a dark-matter search result meeting physics-community standards. This connects algorithm development with the downstream scientific analysis.

The contribution is an experimental data resource and evaluation pathway, rather than a reported detection of dark matter. The abstract explicitly states that ABRACADABRA has not made a discovery, although it has produced established search results. TIDMAD enables AI researchers to test whether their denoising methods can extract relevant signals and contribute to publishable physics results using data from an actual experiment.
neurips-2025-tidmad-time-series-dataset-.tldr: TIDMAD provides experimental time series, denoising benchmarks, and a physics analysis pipeline for applying AI to dark-matter searches.

paragraphs: Text-to-image systems often use several safeguards in sequence, including prompt screening, concept removal, and output-image filtering. An attack that defeats one component may still be stopped by another. This paper examines whether overlapping weaknesses across these layers can allow the complete protection system to be bypassed.

The proposed Transstratal Adversarial Attack is a black-box framework that searches for prompts affecting all defense layers together. At a high level, it combines language-model-generated candidates with genetic optimization to search for successful attacks. The research focuses on the combined behavior of the safeguards, showing why studying each component in isolation can miss weaknesses that appear across the full pipeline.

Evaluation spans 14 text-to-image models and 17 safety modules. The authors report an average attack success rate of 85.6% and a 73.5% improvement over state-of-the-art methods, as expressed in the abstract. They also introduce a benchmark for holistic robustness evaluation. These findings challenge the assumption that separately designed safeguards necessarily provide strong protection when composed into a multilayer system.
neurips-2025-transstratal-adversarial-at.tldr: TAA exposes overlapping weaknesses in multilayer text-to-image safeguards, motivating evaluation of the complete defense pipeline.

paragraphs: Conditional average treatment effects estimate how an intervention's average impact varies with observed characteristics. A common decision rule chooses the intervention when its estimated effect is positive. This paper shows that an estimator can be optimal at predicting treatment-effect values yet still be suboptimal for making decisions with that rule.

The analysis focuses on two-stage estimators such as the DR-learner. Their estimation objectives can prioritize accuracy far from the decision boundary, where changing the estimated magnitude may leave the chosen action unchanged. Errors near the boundary matter differently because they can change which action is selected. This creates a mismatch between accurate effect estimation and good decision performance.

The authors propose a two-stage learning objective that retargets treatment-effect estimation to balance these concerns. A neural method optimizes an adaptively smoothed approximation of the objective. The paper supports the method both theoretically and empirically. Its central implication is that the purpose of an estimate should shape its training objective: when estimates drive decisions, optimizing numerical accuracy alone may not produce the best choices.
neurips-2025-treatment-effect-estimation.tldr: Treatment-effect estimators can make suboptimal decisions despite optimal estimation accuracy; a retargeted objective better balances both goals.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can produce strong image super-resolution results, but their repeated generation steps are expensive. Existing one-step approaches often learn from a multistep teacher, which can limit their quality when that teacher is insufficiently capable. D³SR addresses this issue with a one-step model trained using a larger diffusion discriminator.

The discriminator draws on noisy latent features from any diffusion timestep. This supplies training information intended to overcome potential restrictions imposed by relying on a teacher model's capabilities. The method also introduces an edge-aware version of the DISTS perceptual loss, giving training additional guidance for generating fine details.

Experiments report quantitative and qualitative results comparable to or better than earlier diffusion methods that require dozens or hundreds of steps. Relative to the compared methods, D³SR achieves at least three times faster inference and uses at least 30% fewer parameters. The findings support the paper's central approach: a stronger discriminator and detail-sensitive training objective can help a one-step super-resolution model retain quality while reducing generation cost.
neurips-2025-unleashing-the-power-of-one.tldr: D³SR uses a large diffusion discriminator and edge-aware perceptual loss to deliver high-quality one-step super-resolution with faster inference.
